# 2 Baruch Chapter 1 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 1:1 — Opening formula and dating formula

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "And-it-came-to-pass in-the-twenty-and-fifth year" | Preserves Syriac waw-consecutive and construct chain literally |
| LOGOS | "And it came to pass in the twenty-fifth year" | Formal English preserving syntax and narrative register |
| PNEUMA | "In the twenty-fifth year of King Jeconiah" | Drops narrative formula; streamlines for modern readers |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. The formula "and it came to pass" is a genuine Syriac narrative marker worth preserving. PNEUMA's omission loses the apocalyptic narrative voice. EMET's hyphenation is unnecessary in this phrase.

---

## 1:2 — "greater are they" — comparison of sins

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "greater [are they] than the-ten-tribes" | Bracketed implied copula; literal word order |
| LOGOS | "They are greater than the ten tribes" | Smooth formal English |
| PNEUMA | "The two tribes who stayed behind are worse than the ten" | Interpretive — "worse" for "greater [in sin]" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. "Greater" in context clearly refers to greater in evil/sin. PNEUMA's "worse" is interpretively correct but loses the rhetorical weight of "greater." EMET's brackets are helpful but unnecessary in consensus.

---

## 1:4 — "removed from before my face for a season"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "it-shall-be-removed from-before my-face for-a-season" | Literal Syriac idiom preserved |
| LOGOS | "it shall be removed from before my face for a season" | Formal, preserves idiom |
| PNEUMA | "For a time it will be hidden from my sight" | "Hidden" for "removed"; "my sight" for "my face" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. "Removed from before my face" is the established biblical idiom. PNEUMA's "hidden" shifts the agency; EMET and LOGOS both correctly retain the divine perspective.

---

**Total disagreements this chapter: 3**
